commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When no precision is in effect, out_string() already knows the exact
string length, so emit it directly through stream_run() instead of
scanning the string a second time in stream_zrun().

A negative precision means "no precision" (C treats it as omitted), so
it takes the same direct path as the unbounded case. Only an explicit,
non-negative precision keeps the bounded, NUL-aware scan, since there the
string may be shorter than the precision or the buffer may not be
NUL-terminated.

Closes #23019

(cherry picked from commit aad438d53569de2f29a54f6c65755fb0e7f0ed8f)

tidy-up: null-terminator, NUL byte

Minor steps to improve consistency.

Prefer 'null-terminator', NUL (uppercase) byte, null (lowercase) byte.
Perfer NUL over zero.

While here, drop the redundant negative-precision re-check in formatf():
out_string() already treats any negative precision as if it were omitted,
so rewriting a negative precision parameter to -1 beforehand no longer
changes the result.

Closes #23201

(cherry picked from commit 60cf74f438cfaa4cbf133b1a5f712225a787783c)

coupling:
The reachable out-of-bounds read exists only when BOTH edited commits are present; each diff is correct maintenance on its own.

bd14bfd (edit-A) adds the fast, non-NUL-scanning string emitter and selects it with `if(prec < 0)` instead of `if(prec == -1)`, justified as 'a negative precision means no precision'. This is behavior-preserving in isolation: the only way a negative-but-not-(-1) precision can reach out_string() is via the `%.*s` precision argument, and at that time formatf() still clamps any negative `%.*s` precision to -1 (so prec is always -1 for the fast path and len == strlen). Non-negative precisions still take the bounded stream_zrun() scan. With edit-A alone the PoC prints the whole string and does not fire.

d30f712 (edit-B) drops the formatf() clamp that rewrote a negative `%.*s` precision parameter to -1, justified as redundant because 'out_string() already treats any negative precision as omitted' (which is exactly what edit-A made true). In isolation (on top of the real bd14bfd, whose selector is still `prec == -1`), an unclamped negative precision computes len = (size_t)prec (huge) but is routed to stream_zrun(), which stops at the NUL and stays in bounds. With edit-B alone the PoC does not fire.

Only composed do the two gaps line up: edit-B lets a negative precision (e.g. -8 from `%.*s`) reach out_string() unclamped, where len becomes (size_t)-8; edit-A's broadened `prec < 0` selector then routes that length into the raw stream_run()/memcpy path, reading ~SIZE_MAX bytes from the source string -> heap-buffer-overflow read.

A correct fix must reason across both commits: restoring the clamp alone undoes d30f712's cleanup, and tightening the selector alone undoes bd14bfd's intent; the real invariant (a negative precision must be normalized to the unbounded length BEFORE the raw emitter is chosen) spans both edits, and the `len = (size_t)prec` computation they jointly expose.
